claims.text: As-received Q235 steel in its typical rolled condition has a heterogeneous distribution of carbides along grain boundaries.
Controlled annealing of Q235 steel promotes coalescence of carbides at grain boundaries.
Coalescence and homogenization of grain-boundary carbides reduce fast oxygen-diffusion pathways.
Reduced oxygen transport enables formation of a more coherent and adherent Fe-oxide scale on Q235 steel.
A coherent protective oxide scale can hinder further oxidation by acting as a diffusion barrier.
Fe3O4 is an example of the protective Fe-oxide scale expected on annealed Q235 steel.
The heterogeneous carbide distribution in as-received Q235 produces a less uniform oxide layer.
The oxide layer on as-received Q235 is more prone to spallation and accelerated high-temperature degradation.
A 75 wt.% Na2SO4 and 25 wt.% NaCl mixture is relevant to hot-corrosion testing at 900 °C.
The cited high-entropy-alloy study investigated AlCoCrFeNi2.1-based coatings under the specified mixed molten salt at 900 °C.
Annealed Q235 will show reduced mass loss relative to as-received Q235 during high-temperature salt exposure.
Annealed Q235 will experience fewer oxide-scale spallation events than as-received Q235 during high-temperature salt exposure.
Annealed Q235 will have lower localized corrosion rates than as-received Q235 during high-temperature salt exposure.
Room-temperature oxidation kinetics are sufficiently slow that annealed and untreated samples should show only subtle differences.
The proposed protective mechanism is significant only above 700 °C in salt-rich corrosive environments.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when the steel composition differs significantly from Q235.
Comparing as-received Q235 with Q235 annealed at 700 °C for varied durations can isolate the role of annealing-induced carbide evolution.

Failure of annealed samples to show statistically significant improvements in oxide-scale coherency, mass loss, and localized corrosion rate would falsify carbide coalescence as the governing mediator.

contradictions.description: The experiment and predictions treat 700–900 °C as the high-temperature regime, while the boundary says the mechanism is significant only above 700 °C, which excludes the proposed 700 °C endpoint.
